question: Which of these are classified as micronutrients?
explanation: Great job! Vitamins and minerals are our micronutrients—we only need them in small amounts, but they do big things for our bodies. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h1)

question: What do we mean by the term 'hidden hunger'?

options.A: People hide their food insecurity out of shame in rural communities
options.B: Individuals consume adequate calories but lack essential vitamins and minerals
options.C: Food items lose their nutrients completely during traditional cooking
options.D: Laboratory tests cannot detect nutritional shortages in the early stages

explanation: Spot on! 'Hidden hunger' happens when someone gets enough food to feel full (calories), but their body is starving for vital vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h1)

question: A shortage of which mineral leads to an enlarged thyroid gland, known as a goiter?
explanation: You got it! Iodine helps the thyroid gland make important hormones. Without enough iodine, the thyroid swells up, causing a goiter. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h2)

question: A young child comes in with frequent diarrhea, slow growth, and wounds that take too long to heal. Which deficiency is most likely the cause?
explanation: Well done! Zinc is a superstar for a child's immune system, gut health, and growth. When it's low, healing and recovery slow down. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h2)

question: In many poor communities, what is the main dietary cause of micronutrient deficiencies?

options.A: High intake of dairy products and fresh vegetables
options.B: Frequent eating of high-protein animal meals
options.C: Heavy reliance on a single starchy staple food
options.D: Excessive consumption of imported canned foods

explanation: Correct! Eating only one starchy food day in and day out means the body misses out on the wide variety of nutrients it needs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h3)

question: How do tummy bugs and intestinal worms make malnutrition worse?

options.A: By forcing the body to store excess water instead of vitamins
options.B: By changing the genetic makeup of digestive enzymes
options.C: By reducing nutrient absorption and increasing physical loss of nutrients
options.D: By completely eliminating the sensation of hunger

explanation: Spot on! Parasites damage the lining of the gut, making it hard to absorb food and often causing blood or nutrient loss. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which eye sign is a classic warning sign of advanced Vitamin A deficiency?
explanation: You're right! Bitot's spots look like little foamy, dry patches on the white part of the eye, telling us the child badly needs Vitamin A. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why does a person with iron deficiency anemia look so pale?

options.A: Lack of iron thickens the outer layer of the skin
options.B: Poor circulation causes blood to pool exclusively in deep organs
options.C: Reduced hemoglobin levels decrease the red color of the blood and skin
options.D: The liver stops producing melanin pigments in the skin

explanation: Correct! Hemoglobin is what gives blood its bright red color. When iron is low, hemoglobin drops, and the skin loses that healthy pinkish glow. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h4)

question: What simple tool do community health nurses use to quickly screen children for acute malnutrition?
explanation: Spot on! The MUAC tape is a nurse's best friend in the field—it's quick, easy, and gives a reliable check on a child's wasting status. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the main goal of doing a dietary assessment in a community?

options.A: To understand the regular food intake and eating patterns of families
options.B: To calculate the exact financial income of every household
options.C: To determine the water sanitation index of the village
options.D: To diagnose infectious diseases like malaria and typhoid

explanation: Great! By asking about what families normally eat, nurses can spot missing nutrients and help plan practical solutions. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h5)

question: What does food fortification mean?

options.A: Adding essential vitamins and minerals to commonly eaten foods during processing
options.B: Storing harvested grains in airtight silos to prevent insect damage
options.C: Cooking traditional meals with extra salt and local spices
options.D: Growing crops using chemical fertilizers to increase crop yield

explanation: You got it! Fortification is like a health boost added right into everyday foods (like flour or salt) to protect whole communities from deficiencies. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which public health intervention quickly protects young children against severe Vitamin A deficiency during immunisation drives?

options.A: Teaching mothers how to boil drinking water

explanation: Spot on! Giving high-dose Vitamin A capsules during routine immunization outreach is a fast, effective way to keep kids protected. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the best feeding practice recommended for an infant's first six months of life?
explanation: Correct! Breast milk alone provides all the water, nutrients, and antibodies a baby needs for the first six months. Nothing else is required! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why do community nurses love using practical cooking demonstrations with local foods?

options.A: They allow the nurse to sell cooking utensils to rural women
options.B: They show caregivers how to prepare affordable, nutrient-dense meals using familiar ingredients
options.C: They replace the need for hospital-based medical treatments entirely
options.D: They prove that imported foreign foods are superior to local produce

explanation: Well done! Cooking demos turn nutrition tips into real-life kitchen skills using food that families can easily find and afford locally. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h7)
